youtube.title: What does sound look like? Sand on a vibrating plate 🔊 #shorts
youtube.description:
Sand on a metal plate. When the plate sings, the sand jumps away from the parts that move and gathers on the lines that stand still. Every new note draws a new figure: Chladni figures, first seen in 1787.

A sound wave stands still in each tube. Dust is pushed away where the air moves and piles up where it stays still. Tube k plays harmonic k, so it gets k + 1 piles.

hook.text: Why does a clarinet sound different?

youtube.title: A tube closed at one end skips every other note 🎷 #shorts
youtube.description:
Close one end of a tube and it can only sing the odd harmonics: 1, 3, 5, 7 … That is why a clarinet sounds hollow. The dust shows each standing wave.

#satisfying #simulation #shorts

youtube.title: The double slit, drawn by sand 🌊 #shorts
youtube.description:
Two sources side by side send out the same wave. Where the waves meet in step they add up; where they meet out of step they cancel, and the sand gathers on those lines. Shorter waves, more lines.

#satisfying #simulation #shorts
youtube.tags: double slit, interference, waves, physics, education, satisfying, shorts

youtube.title: Six speakers aim one beam 📡 #shorts
youtube.description:
Six sources in a row. Give each one a small head start (a phase that grows with j) and their waves add up in a slanted beam. That is how phased-array radar and 5G antennas steer without moving.

#satisfying #simulation #shorts
